source_text: The legislation framed the procedure as a violation of children's bodily integrity and rights under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, garnering support from hundreds of Icelandic medical professionals, including doctors and nurses who argued it constituted unnecessary genital mutilation without medical justification.
